title: Car Accident FNOL – Standard Operating Procedure
content:
Super Insurance – Car Accident First Notice of Loss (FNOL)

Procedure:
1. Confirm the safety of all parties involved in the accident.
2. Record the date, time, and specific location of the incident.
3. Obtain a brief description of how the accident occurred.
4. Determine whether the vehicle is drivable or requires towing.
5. Advise the caller not to admit fault to any other parties at the scene.
6. If a police report was filed, collect the report number.
7. Inform the caller that a claims adjuster will contact them within 24-48 hours to assess the damage and guide next steps.
8. This procedure covers the initial property damage and liability claim intake.

title: Towing & Rental Coverage Policy
content:
Super Insurance – Towing & Vehicle Replacement Coverage

Coverage Rules:
- Towing and Roadside Assistance is included with Comprehensive policies and the Roadside Assistance add-on.
- Covered towing is authorized up to ₹12,000 per incident.
- Rental vehicle reimbursement is available only with the Rental Reimbursement add-on (₹3,000/day for up to 30 days).
- Third-Party Only liability policies do not include towing, roadside, or rental coverage.
- For uncovered policyholders, towing and rental services can still be arranged but are billed directly to the customer as out-of-pocket expenses.

title: Vehicle Vandalism Claims
content:
Super Insurance – Vandalism Claim Procedure

Procedure:
1. A police report is required for all vandalism claims.
2. Document the type of damage: keyed paint, broken windows, slashed tires, graffiti, etc.
3. Vandalism falls under Comprehensive coverage. The policyholder must hold a Comprehensive policy for the claim to be valid.
4. The standard Comprehensive deductible applies (typically ₹10,000 or ₹25,000).
5. Photographs of the damage are required (minimum 4 angles).
6. An adjuster visit will be scheduled, or the caller may visit an approved repair facility.
7. Filing a vandalism claim generally does not affect the policyholder's premium.

title: Life Insurance Death Claim – Filing Procedures
content:
Super Insurance – Life Insurance Death Claim Procedure

Procedure:
1. Express condolences to the caller sincerely and professionally.
2. Locate the policy using the policy number or the registered phone number.
3. Verify the caller's full legal name against the beneficiary records on file.
4. Record the following details about the insured's passing:
   - Date of death
   - Location of death
   - Cause of death
5. Required documents for claim processing:
   - Certified death certificate (original or certified copy)
   - Completed beneficiary claim form (to be mailed or emailed to the caller)
   - Government-issued photo ID of the claimant (copy)
6. Payout timeline: Claims are typically processed within 30-60 days after all documents are received.
7. Payout options available: lump sum, installments, or annuity.
8. If the death occurred within the 2-year contestability period, the claim is subject to additional review by the Underwriting department.

title: Fraud Indicators – Red Flags Reference Guide
content:
Super Insurance – Fraud Detection Reference

Common Red Flags:
- Claim filed immediately after policy inception or a recent coverage increase
- Caller demonstrates unusual familiarity with the claims process
- Description of events sounds inconsistent or rehearsed
- Incident occurred in a remote location with no witnesses
- Caller is pressuring for an expedited settlement
- Vehicle was recently listed for sale prior to a theft claim
- Comprehensive coverage was recently added before a theft or vandalism claim
- Multiple prior claims filed within a short period

Protocol: If any red flags are observed, document them in the claim notes and flag the file for SIU (Special Investigations Unit) review. Do not confront or accuse the caller.

title: Medical Insurance Hospitalization Claim – Standard Operating Procedure
content:
Super Insurance – Medical Insurance Hospitalization Claim SOP

Procedure:
1. Confirm whether the policyholder or covered family member has been admitted to a hospital or is scheduled for admission.
2. Determine if the hospital is in the network (cashless eligible) or out-of-network (reimbursement only).
3. For CASHLESS claims:
   a. Verify the hospital is in the policyholder's network list.
   b. A pre-authorization request must be submitted by the hospital to Super Insurance's TPA (Third Party Administrator) within 24 hours of admission.
   c. Inform the caller that the hospital's insurance desk will handle the pre-authorization paperwork.
   d. Pre-authorization approval is typically communicated within 2-4 hours for planned admissions, and within 1 hour for emergencies.
   e. The policyholder only pays the copay percentage and any amounts exceeding sub-limits.
4. For REIMBURSEMENT claims:
   a. The policyholder pays the hospital bill upfront.
   b. Required documents for reimbursement: original hospital bills, discharge summary, diagnostic reports, doctor's prescription, pharmacy bills, and completed claim form.
   c. All documents must be submitted within 15 days of discharge.
   d. Reimbursement is processed within 30 days of receiving complete documentation.
5. IRDAI requires that the insurer must be intimated within 24 hours of hospitalization for planned admissions and within 48 hours for emergency admissions.
6. Room rent and ICU charges are subject to sub-limits as per the policy. Inform the caller of their applicable sub-limits.
7. A claims coordinator will be assigned and will contact the policyholder within 24 hours to guide next steps.

title: Pre-Existing Conditions & Waiting Period Policy
content:
Super Insurance – Pre-Existing Conditions & Waiting Period Policy

Policy Rules:
1. Pre-existing conditions (PED) are covered only after the mandatory waiting period of 4 years from the policy inception date.
2. Common pre-existing conditions include: diabetes, hypertension, thyroid disorders, asthma, heart conditions, and kidney disease.
3. If the waiting period has NOT expired, claims related to the pre-existing condition are excluded. The policyholder must be informed clearly and sensitively.
4. If the waiting period HAS expired, the pre-existing condition is treated as any other covered illness — standard claim procedures apply.
5. Specific disease waiting period: Certain conditions (e.g., hernia, cataracts, joint replacement, kidney stones) have a separate 2-year specific disease waiting period regardless of pre-existing status.
6. Non-disclosure of pre-existing conditions at policy inception may result in claim rejection. If non-disclosure is suspected, flag the claim for underwriting review.
7. The copay percentage may be higher for claims related to pre-existing conditions — check the policy terms.
8. IRDAI mandates that all waiting period exclusions must be clearly communicated to the policyholder at the time of claim intimation.

title: Day-Care & OPD Claim Procedures
content:
Super Insurance – Day-Care & OPD Claim Procedures

Day-Care Procedures:
1. Day-care procedures are medical treatments or surgeries that require less than 24 hours of hospitalization.
2. Common covered day-care procedures: cataract surgery, dialysis, chemotherapy, lithotripsy, tonsillectomy, dental surgery under general anesthesia, and arthroscopy.
3. Day-care claims follow the same cashless/reimbursement process as regular hospitalization claims.
4. Pre-authorization is required for cashless day-care procedures — the hospital's insurance desk should initiate this.
5. The policyholder must have the 'Day-Care Procedures' add-on or comprehensive coverage that includes day-care benefits.

OPD (Outpatient) Claims:
1. OPD benefits cover doctor consultations, diagnostic tests, pharmacy bills, and minor procedures that do not require hospitalization.
2. OPD is covered ONLY if the policyholder has the 'OPD Cover' add-on.
3. For OPD claims, the policyholder pays upfront and submits bills for reimbursement.
4. Required documents: doctor's prescription, diagnostic reports, pharmacy bills, and consultation receipts.
5. OPD claims are typically processed within 15 days of document submission.
6. There is usually an annual OPD limit (₹15,000 – ₹25,000 depending on the plan). Inform the caller of their remaining OPD balance.
